name: Rafe Halloway
appearance: teenage human boy of fifteen, gangly and still growing, untidy dark hair, his sister's tired brown eyes, burn-scarred apprentice's gloves tucked in his belt, a soot-streaked smock several sizes too big
role: Glassblower's apprentice on Glassblowers' Row; Jun Halloway's younger brother
portrait: With strangers Rafe is shy for a minute and then can't stop talking, mostly about glass and the Coil Line. With people he knows he's cheeky and loud, and protective of his sister in a way he'd never admit. He notices color, heat, how things are made, and who's looking down on him for his age. He'll talk about the furnaces, the floats in the windows, his master's temper, the Couriers he'd like to run with and Jun's clinic, which he's proud of. He picks at the burn scars on his gloves. When he's caught out he gets loud.

longTerm: Earn enough to help keep Jun's clinic in burn gel
agenda.current: Finish his shift without breaking anything, and get to the Wheelhouse before Jun notices he's gone

contradictions: Hates being looked after, and does exactly what Jun does: looks after everyone
Says glassblowing is boring, and stays late at the furnace every night

sampleLines: You want to see the furnace? Mind your sleeves. Everyone says that, but mind your sleeves.
Jun doesn't need looking after. She just needs burn gel.
The gaffer says I've got good hands and a bad mouth. Both true.

shifts.warm: Shows you the best float in the window
shifts.lying: Talks very fast and too much
shifts.afraid: Goes quiet and stands closer to whoever's oldest

tells: Talks very fast and too much when he's lying

display.grief: works at the furnace until it's dark
display.fear: goes quiet and stays near the oldest person
display.hurt: stops talking to you for a day
display.affection: shows you the best float in the window
display.joy: talks fast and laughs at his own jokes
display.gratitude: says thanks too quickly and looks away

knowledge: His sister Jun works nights at the Wheel clinic; it's out of burn gel again
Odile Marsh, his master, has the best hands on Glassblowers' Row and the worst temper
The Wheelhouse pays a few cinders for short packets across the Wheel, and doesn't ask a runner's age
Teo Varrin studies for the Phoenix Academy from borrowed books; Rafe thinks that's brave

secrets.text: After his shifts he runs short packets across the Wheel for the Wheelhouse, for cinders he puts in the clinic's donation tin. Jun thinks he's asleep.
secrets.summary: Runs packets for the Couriers after his shifts; Jun doesn't know.
secrets.tell: Talks very fast and too much
secrets.revealWhen: Jun is in trouble the cinders could fix

relations.note: she half raised him and still checks he's eaten; he'd do anything for her and will never say so
apprenticed to her for two years; she shouts, and taught him everything
